explanation: Most geometry word problems are really just plugging numbers into a formula. Drag the length and width sliders to reshape the rectangle: its area (the shaded inside) grows as length*width, while its perimeter (the distance the dot walks all the way around) grows as 2*(length+width). Notice that doubling one side doubles the area but only adds to the perimeter — that's why the two answers behave so differently.
bullets: Area = L*W counts the squares INSIDE; perimeter = 2(L+W) measures the border AROUND.
The walking dot traces exactly what 'perimeter' means: once around the whole edge.
Read the problem, match it to the right formula, then substitute the given numbers.
